title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
abstract: arXiv:2610.40532v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How effectively can vision-language-action (VLA) models learn diverse language-conditioned behaviors as training data scales? Investigating this question requires large and varied robot datasets, whose collection on physical robots remains costly. We introduce BURGER, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, both in simulation and the real world. In BURGER, an agent starts from the same blank canvas and controls a robot arm to draw the object or spatial composition specified by language, while each instruction allows an open-ended variety of valid drawings and stroke orders. Using 28,200 simulated demonstrations spanning 282 drawing tasks, we evaluate five representative VLA models across data scales, language grounding, and multimodal behavior. BURGER supports fine-grained analysis of language grounding, spatial composition, and action gene

translated_title: BURGER：通过具身绘图对机器人泛化能力进行基准测试与理解
translated_abstract: 随着训练数据规模的扩大，视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型能够多有效地学习多样化的语言条件行为？研究这一问题需要大规模且多样的机器人数据集，而在真实机器人上采集此类数据的成本依然高昂。我们提出了BURGER，一个以语言为条件的机器人绘图基准，它配备可扩展的、由提示驱动的流水线，可在仿真和现实世界中生成连续的绘图轨迹。在BURGER中，智能体从同一张空白画布出发，控制机械臂绘制语言所指定的物体或空间构图，且每条指令都允许多种开放式的有效绘图结果和笔画顺序。利用覆盖282个绘图任务的28,200条仿真演示数据，我们从数据规模、语言接地和多模态行为等方面评估了五种具有代表性的VLA模型。BURGER支持对语言接地、空间构图和动作生成进行细粒度分析。
tldr: 提出了BURGER——一个语言条件下的机器人绘图基准，通过可扩展的提示驱动流水线生成连续绘图轨迹，用于在数据规模扩大时对VLA模型的泛化能力、语言接地和多模态行为进行细粒度评估。
en_tdlr: We introduce BURGER, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, enabling fine-grained evaluation of VLA models' generalization across data scales, language grounding, and multimodal behavior.
